name: Vaughan's first moment distribution bound for $x\ge10^{52}$: Decomp1525c
description:
This mission concerns an explicit first moment estimate for representations by two odd primes. For a real parameter $x$, the weighted count $\Psi(x)$ assigns weight $\log p_1$ to prime pairs with $3\le p_1\le x-3$ and $x-p_1<p_2\le2x-p_1$. The comparison term is $M(x)=\int_3^x u/\log u\,du+\int_x^{2x}(2x-u)/\log u\,du$. The moving interval sum $I_x(u)$ records the logarithmic weights of admissible primes at a given integration parameter.

The target is $|\Psi(x)-M(x)|<x^2/(5\log^2x)$ for $x\ge10^{52}$, conditional on two explicit inputs: a Chebyshev theta error estimate above $678407$ and a preliminary prime pair integral approximation valid throughout the target range. The individual tasks specify exact identities, integrability assertions, and numerical error estimates. Each hypothesis and constant is retained from the lab file. The assembly statement is included as the mission goal even though its assembly proof already exists in the lab; the ten leaves remain open.

The source is R. C. Vaughan, [On the estimation of Schnirelman's constant](https://doi.org/10.1515/crll.1977.290.93), Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik 290, 1977, pages 93 to 108, specifically page 103 in the proof of Lemma 11. Such explicit estimates support bounds for expressing integers as sums of a bounded number of primes. Binary Goldbach remains open.

These statements come from an AI-run Lean lab, with AI-written Lean code, and were audited by a human before submission. This is a draft for the platform's human audit before submission; it supplies no new proofs.

import Mathlib
open Finset Real MeasureTheory intervalIntegral
open scoped Classical
noncomputable section
namespace LL_Decomp1525c
def P1V (x : ℝ) : Finset ℕ := (Icc 3 ⌊x - 3⌋₊).filter Nat.Prime
end LL_Decomp1525c
items.natural_language_statement: For real $x$, $P_1(x)$ is the finite set of primes $p$ with $3\le p\le\lfloor x-3\rfloor_+$, where $\lfloor\cdot\rfloor_+$ is the natural number floor.

items.definition:
import Mathlib
open Finset Real MeasureTheory intervalIntegral
open scoped Classical
noncomputable section
namespace LL_Decomp1525c
def PsiV (x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ p₁ ∈ (Icc 3 ⌊x - 3⌋₊).filter Nat.Prime,
    ∑ _p₂ ∈ (Icc 1 ⌊2 * x - p₁⌋₊).filter (fun p : ℕ => p.Prime ∧ x - p₁ < (p : ℝ)), Real.log p₁
end LL_Decomp1525c
items.natural_language_statement: For real $x$, $\Psi(x)$ sums $\log p_1$ over prime pairs satisfying $3\le p_1\le\lfloor x-3\rfloor_+$, $1\le p_2\le\lfloor 2x-p_1\rfloor_+$, and $x-p_1<p_2$.

items.definition_title: Main integral for the first moment
items.definition:
import Mathlib
open Finset Real MeasureTheory intervalIntegral
open scoped Classical
noncomputable section
namespace LL_Decomp1525c
def mainIntegralV (x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (∫ u in (3 : ℝ)..x, u / Real.log u) + ∫ u in x..(2 * x), (2 * x - u) / Real.log u
end LL_Decomp1525c
items.natural_language_statement: For real $x$, define $M(x)=\int_3^x u/\log u\,du+\int_x^{2x}(2x-u)/\log u\,du$, using oriented interval integrals.

items.definition:
import Mathlib
import Definitions.Def_LL_Decomp1525c_P1V
open Finset Real MeasureTheory intervalIntegral
open scoped Classical
noncomputable section
namespace LL_Decomp1525c
def thetaI (x u : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ p ∈ (P1V x).filter (fun p : ℕ => x - p < u ∧ u ≤ 2 * x - p), Real.log p
end LL_Decomp1525c
items.natural_language_statement: For real $x,u$, define $I_x(u)=\sum_{p\in P_1(x),\ x-p<u\le2x-p}\log p$.

items.theorem_title: Exchange the prime sum and integral
items.formal_statement:
namespace LL_Decomp1525c
theorem swap (x : ℝ) (hx : 6 ≤ x) :
    ∑ p ∈ P1V x, Real.log p * ∫ u in (x - p)..(2 * x - p), 1 / Real.log u =
      ∫ u in (3 : ℝ)..(2 * x), thetaI x u / Real.log u := by sorry
end LL_Decomp1525c
items.natural_language_statement: For every real $x\ge6$, $\sum_{p\in P_1(x)}\log p\int_{x-p}^{2x-p}du/\log u=\int_3^{2x}I_x(u)/\log u\,du$.

items.theorem_title: Identify the lower interval prime sum
items.formal_statement:
namespace LL_Decomp1525c
theorem thetaI_low (x u : ℝ) (hx : 6 ≤ x) (hu3 : 3 ≤ u) (hux : u ≤ x) :
    thetaI x u = Chebyshev.theta (x - 3) - Chebyshev.theta (max (x - u) 2) := by sorry
end LL_Decomp1525c
items.natural_language_statement: For real $x\ge6$ and $3\le u\le x$, $I_x(u)=\theta(x-3)-\theta(\max(x-u,2))$, where $\theta(t)=\sum_{p\le t}\log p$ over primes.

namespace LL_Decomp1525c
theorem thetaI_high (x u : ℝ) (hx : 6 ≤ x) (hxu : x ≤ u) (hu : u ≤ 2 * x) :
    thetaI x u = max (Chebyshev.theta (min (x - 3) (2 * x - u)) - Real.log 2) 0 := by sorry
end LL_Decomp1525c
items.natural_language_statement: For real $x\ge6$ and $x\le u\le2x$, $I_x(u)=\max(\theta(\min(x-3,2x-u))-\log2,0)$, where $\theta$ is Chebyshev's prime logarithm sum.

items.theorem_title: Bound the lower interval pointwise error
items.formal_statement:
namespace LL_Decomp1525c
theorem low_pointwise
    (h215 : ∀ y : ℝ, 678407 ≤ y → |Chebyshev.theta y - y| < y / (40 * Real.log y))
    (x u : ℝ) (hx : 10 ^ 52 ≤ x) (hu3 : 3 ≤ u) (hux : u ≤ x) :
    |thetaI x u - u| ≤ x / (40 * Real.log x)
      + max (x - u) 2 / (40 * Real.log (max (x - u) 2)) + 678412 := by sorry
end LL_Decomp1525c
items.natural_language_statement: Assume $|\theta(y)-y|<y/(40\log y)$ for every real $y\ge678407$, where $\theta$ is Chebyshev's prime logarithm sum. For real $x\ge10^{52}$ and $3\le u\le x$, with $t=\max(x-u,2)$, $|I_x(u)-u|\le x/(40\log x)+t/(40\log t)+678412$.

namespace LL_Decomp1525c
theorem distribution_of
    (h215 : ∀ y : ℝ, 678407 ≤ y → |Chebyshev.theta y - y| < y / (40 * Real.log y))
    (hPI : ∀ x : ℝ, 10 ^ 52 ≤ x →
      |PsiV x - ∑ p ∈ P1V x, Real.log p * ∫ u in (x - p)..(2 * x - p), 1 / Real.log u|
        < x ^ 2 / (12 * Real.log x ^ 2)) :
    ∀ x : ℝ, 10 ^ 52 ≤ x → |PsiV x - mainIntegralV x| < x ^ 2 / (5 * Real.log x ^ 2) := by sorry
end LL_Decomp1525c
items.natural_language_statement: Assume $|\theta(y)-y|<y/(40\log y)$ for every real $y\ge678407$, where $\theta$ is Chebyshev's prime logarithm sum. Also assume that for every real $z\ge10^{52}$, $|\Psi(z)-\sum_{p\in P_1(z)}\log p\int_{z-p}^{2z-p}du/\log u|<z^2/(12\log^2z)$. Conditional on these two inputs, every real $x\ge10^{52}$ satisfies $|\Psi(x)-M(x)|<x^2/(5\log^2x)$.
